courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Balancing the Environment: Science, Human Values, and Policy in North Carolina
courses.description: This course examines the ways in which scientific information, human values, and the policy process interact to produce environmental change, economic growth, and social justice in North Carolina.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: First Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Global Environmental Change
courses.description: Interdisciplinary course exploring the intersection between the natural world and society. Students will learn about how natural systems work, the ecosystem services they provide to societies, how global change has impacted these services on local and global scales, and how science is used to find solutions to these problems and inform environmental policy.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Our Energy and Climate Crises: Challenges and Opportunities
courses.description: Students quantify global depletion of energy resources and accompanying environmental degradation, hence discovering the profound changes in attitudes and behavior required to adjust to diminished fossil fuels and modified climate.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Special Topics in Environmental Science and Studies, FC-PAST
courses.description: Topics from diverse areas of environmental science and/or environmental studies are explored.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Introduction to Environment and Society
courses.description: Human-environment interactions are examined through analytical methods from the social sciences, humanities, and sciences. The focus is on the role of social, political, and economic factors in controlling interactions between society and the environment in historical and cultural contexts. Three lecture hours and one recitation hour a week. Honors version available.
courses.gen_ed_raw: FY-LAUNCH (only designated sections), FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER.

source.text: ENEC 201. | 4 Credits. | FY-LAUNCH (only designated sections), FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Introduction to the Environmental Sciences
courses.description: This course explores how Earth's natural systems work, emphasizing the ecological processes that confer resilience. Students examine how these systems respond to global change, gaining insight into the science behind ecosystem stability. Students will examine these environmental problems through an interdisciplinary lens by investigating how economic, social, and political frameworks inform conservation and restoration efforts, by applying quantitative tools and methods from non-science disciplines to synthesize information and develop a holistic understanding of complex environmental challenges.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Science Problem Solving
courses.description: A quantitative introduction to selected topics in environmental sciences with an emphasis on developing and solidifying problem-solving skills.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, MATH 231.

source.text: ENEC 203. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, MATH 231 . | FC-NATSCI or FC-QUANT.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Seminar
courses.description: This course will provide an intellectual focus on the interface between environment and society by examining the relationship among science, policy, and actual management practices on a chosen topic.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Humanities
courses.description: While scientific research and technological innovation are critical to addressing the ecological challenges of our time, the environmental humanities can offer equally vital insights by examining how cultural values, artistic expressions, and ethical perspectives have formed -- and been formed by -- humans' relationships with the environment. By consulting artists, poets, writers, and thinkers, students will untangle the intertwined connection between ''nature'' and ''culture,'' tapping into key existential questions about what it means to be humans who not only live in this world, but who seek to solve the environmental problems that they have caused or exacerbated.

source.text: ENEC 205. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING. | FOLK 205 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: New Frontiers: Environment and Society in the United States
courses.description: By employing a multidisciplinary approach, this class will give students a sense of the role that the environment has played in shaping United States society and the role that our society plays in producing environmental change at the national and global level. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Energy in a Sustainable Environment Seminar
courses.description: This seminar series will provide a general introduction to energy sources, resources, technologies, and societal use from a sustainability perspective.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: North Carolina Estuaries: Environmental Processes and Problems
courses.description: Natural processes and human impacts on estuarine systems using the Neuse River estuary as a case study. Course includes one week of intensive field work based at the Institute of Marine Sciences. A student may not receive credit for this course after receiving credit for ENEC 222 . Course previously offered as MASC 220.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Estuarine and Coastal Marine Science
courses.description: Introduction to the estuarine and coastal environment: geomorphology, physical circulation, nutrient loading, primary and secondary production, carbon and nitrogen cycling, benthic processes, and sedimentation. Consideration given to human impact on coastal systems with emphasis on North Carolina estuaries and sounds. Includes a mandatory weekend field trip and laboratory.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, MATH 231 and either CHEM 101 or PHYS 114.

source.text: ENEC 222. | 4 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 231 and either CHEM 101 or PHYS 114 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Food, Environment, and Sustainability
courses.description: Explores the nexus of agricultural, ecological, and food systems as they dynamically interact. The class examines case studies from North Carolina and other parts of the world. Themes include nutrition, food security, agroecology, and sustainable livelihoods. Students engage in readings, class projects, and hands-on activities in a laboratory setting.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Human Ecology of Africa
courses.description: Course examines human adaptations to environments across Africa. Focuses on livelihood systems such as farming, herding and hunting/gathering.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Energy and Culture Seminar for the Thailand Field Site
courses.description: This one credit hour course meets the semester before UNC students go to study abroad at the Institute for the Environment Thailand Field Site. The course will prepare students for the research portion of the program. Student should be applying to the field site when taking this course.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Ecology and Culture Seminar for Ecuador Field Site
courses.description: This one credit hour seminar is only open to students who are planning to participate in the spring research semester in Ecuador. The main purpose of this seminar is to prepare students for this six-month experience in Ecuador by discussing both research methods and Ecuadorian society.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Introduction to Atmospheric Processes
courses.description: Includes one-hour laboratory. Atmospheric processes including radiation, dynamics, and thermodynamics are emphasized. Circulations across a range of temporal and spatial scales are described. Links between environmental problems and the atmosphere are explored.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, MATH 231 and either CHEM 102 or PHYS 114.

source.text: ENEC 253. | 4 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 231 and either CHEM 102 or PHYS 114 . | GEOG 253 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: International Environmental Politics
courses.description: Covers the politics of environmental issues, with a focus on issues that have become internationalized. It focuses on the special problems that arise in creating rules for environmental management and regulation when no single government has authority to enforce those rules.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Mountain Biodiversity
courses.description: Introduction to the new field of biodiversity studies, which integrates approaches from systematics, ecology, evolution, and conservation. Taught at off-campus field station.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Coral Reef Ecology and Management
courses.description: The course familiarizes students with the natural history, ecology, and physical and chemical characteristics of the coral reef environment. Policy and management issues are also examined.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Field Studies in Siberia
courses.description: This course explores the biogeography of Siberia and gives students practical training on how to do field work in field ecology and physical geography.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Conservation of Biodiversity in Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course will give students a multidisciplinary introduction to growing field of biodiversity preservation.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ENEC 201; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: ENEC 264. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENEC 201 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | GEOG 264 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Contemporary Africa: Issues in Health, Population, and the Environment
courses.description: A seminar that introduces students to non-Western perspectives and comparative study of ecological, social, and economic factors that influence the welfare of contemporary African communities. Examination of famine, population growth, and health issues within the context of African cultural and social systems.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Local Flora
courses.description: Open to all undergraduates. North Carolina's flora: recognition, identification, classification, evolution, history, economics, plant families, ecology, and conservation. Three lecture hours per week.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, BIOL 101, and 101L or 102L; Corequisite, BIOL 272L.

source.text: ENEC 272. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, BIOL 101 , and 101L or 102L ; Corequisite, BIOL 272L . | BIOL 272 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Local Flora Lab
courses.description: Open to all undergraduates. North Carolina's flora: recognition, identification, classification, evolution, history, economics, plant families, ecology, and conservation. Three laboratory hours per week.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, BIOL 101, and 101L or 102L; Corequisite, BIOL 272.

source.text: ENEC 272L. | 1 Credits. | Prerequisites, BIOL 101 , and 101L or 102L ; Corequisite, BIOL 272 . | BIOL 272L .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Fungi: Architects of Ecosystems and Sustainable Futures
courses.description: Fungi are an immensely diverse kingdom essential to life, acting as the primary decomposers in all ecosystems. They are ecologically vital as symbionts and pathogens, profoundly impacting plants and animals. Humanity's relationship with fungi spans history, using them for food and fermentation, and increasingly for advanced medicines and sustainable materials. This course surveys fungal biology, covering diversity, evolution, and core traits. The goal is to explore how applied fungal biology and modern trends--including materials science, nanotechnology, metabolic engineering, and alternative proteins--can benefit humanity and promote global sustainability.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, BIOL 101 or ENEC 202.

source.text: ENEC 280. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, BIOL 101 or ENEC 202.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Special Topics in Environmental Science and Studies, FC-GLOBAL
courses.description: Topics from diverse areas of environmental science and/or environmental studies are explored.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Restoration Ecology
courses.description: Explores ecological theory and its application to the restoration of terrestrial, aquatic, and marine ecosystems. Requires 30 hours of service to a local restoration project in which students will collect ecological data for a final case study project.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, BIOL 201 or ENEC 202.

source.text: ENEC 304. | 4 Credits. | Prerequisite, BIOL 201 or ENEC 202.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Data Analysis and Visualization of Social and Environmental Interactions
courses.description: Principles of spatial and temporal data analysis are applied to issues of the role of society in producing environmental change. Methods include statistical analysis, model development, and computer visualization. Three lecture hours and one laboratory hour a week.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ECON 400, ENEC 201, MATH 231, or STOR 155.

source.text: ENEC 305. | 4 Credits. | Prerequisite, ECON 400 , ENEC 201 , MATH 231 , or STOR 155 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Energy and Material Flows in the Environment and Society
courses.description: Examines regional to global scale flow of materials and energy through materials extractions, processing, manufacturing, product use, recycling, and disposal, including relevance to policy development. Reviews natural cycles, basic physics, and technology of energy production.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, ENEC 201 and MATH 231 or MATH 152; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental History
courses.description: Historical development of the system of beliefs, values, institutions, etc, underlying societal response to the environment in different cultures is analyzed. The approach is interdisciplinary, drawing on methods from history, philosophy, psychology, etc. Three lecture hours a week.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Values and Valuation
courses.description: Introduction to the methods for assigning value to aspects of the environment and to interhuman and human-environment interactions. The approach is interdisciplinary, drawing on methods from philosophy, ecology, psychology, aesthetics, economics, religion, etc. Online course.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Coastal Environmental Change
courses.description: An exploration of the large-scale evolution of coastal environments, including relevance of geologic setting, wave and sediment transport processes, the evolution of beach and barrier island morphology, and issues of coastal environmental management. Course previously offered as GEOL 310/MASC 316.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EMES 101, 103, 200, 201, or 401; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: ENEC 310. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, EMES 101 , 103 , 200 , 201 , or 401; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | EMES 310 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Risk-Based International Environmental Decisions
courses.description: A Web-based course on the methods and roles of risk assessment in the international setting, with a primary focus on United States-European Union applications in environmental policy decisions.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: The Future of Energy
courses.description: This course takes a deep dive into the global energy transition, studying the rapidly-evolving renewable energy and energy-efficiency technologies, prices for new energy sources like solar and wind, and competition with fossil and nuclear fuels. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Water in Our World: Introduction to Hydrologic Science and Environmental Problems
courses.description: This introductory course will cover two broad themes: the physical processes of the hydrologic cycle and how human use (and abuse) of freshwater resources can lead to major environmental problems. PX credit for ENEC/ EMES 324 + 324L . PL credit for ENEC/ EMES 324 . Course previously offered as GEOL 324.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Water in Our World Laboratory
courses.description: Students will conduct laboratory and field experiments to reinforce the topics covered in ENEC/GEOL 324. PX credit for ENEC/ EMES 324 + 324L . Course previously offered as GEOL 324L.
courses.requisites_raw: Pre- or corequisite, ENEC/GEOL 324.

source.text: ENEC 324L. | 1 Credits. | Pre- or corequisite, ENEC/GEOL 324. | FC-LAB. | EMES 324L .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Water Resource Management for Food, Energy, and Health
courses.description: This course explores logistical, political, social, and economic challenges in supplying every human with adequate access to clean water. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Principles of Sustainability
courses.description: This course introduces students to theories, principles, and measurement of sustainability. It also provides an overview of sustainability in national and international contexts. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Applications of Drones
courses.description: This course explores the ways Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS, aka ''drones'') are used to view and map our world for managing environment and natural resources. Students will learn how drone imagery is used to solve environmental problems, gain the knowledge necessary to obtain a drone pilots license, get hands-on experience planning missions and flying drones to gather imaging data, and process this imagery with software to produce geospatial products.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Law and Policy
courses.description: This course gives students an overview of environmental law and some practical experience in environmental policy making.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Coastal Law and Policy
courses.description: The utilization of common coastal resources, the management of fisheries, and coastal zone management guide an examination of coastal laws, policies, and regulations at the federal, state, and local levels. Taught at off-campus field station.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Marine Fisheries Ecology
courses.description: Gives students a foundation in population biology and the ecological processes that influence populations of economically important fish and shellfish. Students will gain practical quantitative skills including statistical analyses, model development, and data visualization. Familiarity with introductory statistics concepts is preferred but not necessary.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EMES 103, 401, or ENEC 202.

source.text: ENEC 352. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, EMES 103 , 401, or ENEC 202. | EMES 352 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Living Things, Wilderness, and Ecosystems: An Introduction to Environmental Ethics
courses.description: The meaning of environmental values and their relation to other values; the ethical status of animals, species, wilderness, and ecosystems; the built environment; environmental justice; ecofeminism; obligations to future generations. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Agriculture and the Environment
courses.description: Introduction to the ecology of agricultural practices and the impact of food production on the environment. Particular attention will be paid to the constraints on agriculture which must be overcome to feed the planet's growing population. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Energy Policy
courses.description: This course will provide an overview of some of the most challenging energy issues of the 21st century and will cover the tools and perspectives necessary to analyze those problems.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Global Environment: Policy Analysis and Solutions
courses.description: Explores linkages among nations, global environmental institutions, and the environmental problems they cause and seek to rectify. Introduces pressing challenges of the global environment such as China and India's energy and climate policies, the environmental impacts of coal, nuclear energy, shale gas and fracking, and marine pollution. Discusses perspectives of nations, the role of financial markets and NGOs, and the international community involved in crafting policy solutions.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Confronting Climate Change in the Anthropocene
courses.description: Climate change-perhaps the defining issue of the 21st century-is a highly complex problem that requires interdisciplinary collaboration to develop policy responses. This course explores the science of climate change and uses theories from multiple disciplines, including law, political science, economics, and earth and atmospheric sciences, to frame solutions to this global challenge. Students will apply quantitative and qualitative tools to understand causes and impacts of climate change, as well as policy responses.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Advocacy
courses.description: Explores rhetorical means of citizen influence of practices affecting our natural and human environment; also, study of communication processes and dilemmas of redress of environmental grievances in communities and workplace.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Economics
courses.description: This course develops a set of core principles that are essential to understand and evaluate environmental policy and renewable resource use. These principles are primarily economic, but our discussion will also include insights from politics and ethics.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ECON 101.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Internship in Sustainability
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. This course provides an internship with an organization on sustainability topics and public engagement. Pass/Fail only.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Research in Environmental Sciences and Studies for Undergraduates
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Research in an area of environmental science or environmental studies.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Directed Readings
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. A specialized selection of readings from the literature of a particular environmental field supervised by a member of the Carolina Environmental Faculty group. Written reports on the readings or a literature review paper will be required. Cannot be used as a course toward the major.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 8 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Chemistry Processes
courses.description: Required preparation, a background in chemistry and mathematics, including ordinary differential equations. Chemical processes occurring in natural and engineered systems: chemical cycles; transport and transformation processes of chemicals in air, water, and multimedia environments; chemical dynamics; thermodynamics; structure/activity relationships.
courses.requisites_raw: Pre- or corequisite, CHEM 261.

source.text: ENEC 403. | 3 Credits. | Pre- or corequisite, CHEM 261 . | ENVR 403 , CHEM 403 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Agent-Based Modeling of Social-Ecological Systems
courses.description: This course exposes students to the potential of using agent-based modeling (ABM) to explore social-ecological system dynamics. ABM is used across the social and natural sciences and students will gain both theoretical and applied knowledge in how to use it. Students will acquire skills in computer-simulation modeling, social-ecological systems, writing code, building models and the quantitative interpretation of results. They will do so using the java-based ABM program NetLogo.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Mountain Preservation
courses.description: Introduces students to approaches used to preserve the natural and cultural heritage of the Southern Appalachians. Taught at off-campus field station.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Atmospheric Processes II
courses.description: Principles of analysis of the atmosphere are applied to the analysis of environmental phenomena. The link between the atmosphere and other environmental compartments is explored through environmental case studies.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Principles of Energy Conversion
courses.description: Recommended preparation, ENEC 201 , and MATH 152 or 231 . This course will get students familiar with the principles governing the conversion of a variety of non-renewable and renewable resources to energy services. Physical, chemical, and biological principles involved in the design and analysis of these systems will be reviewed. The basics of project economics applied to the design of energy conversion systems will also be introduced.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Shallow Geophysics: Geological, Archaeological and Environmental Applications
courses.description: The course focuses on the use of shallow geophysical principles and techniques to address geological, archaeological, and environmental problems. The course will study the strengths and weaknesses of geophysical techniques in various geologic settings and how to collect and interpret field data for defined applications. Written reports and group projects will be required.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Earth Processes in Environmental Systems
courses.description: Principles of geological and related Earth systems sciences are applied to analyses of environmental phenomena. The link between the lithosphere and other environmental compartments is explored through case studies of environmental issues. Three lecture hours and one laboratory hour a week.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, CHEM 102, GEOL 200, and MATH 231; and PHYS 115 or 119; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

source.text: ENEC 410. | 4 Credits. | Prerequisites, CHEM 102 , GEOL 200, and MATH 231 ; and PHYS 115 or 119 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites. | EMES 410 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Oceanic Processes in Environmental Systems
courses.description: Principles of analysis of the ocean, coast, and estuarine environments and the processes that control these environments are applied to the analysis of environmental phenomena. Case studies of environmental issues. Three lecture hours and one laboratory hour a week.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, BIOL 101, CHEM 102, ENEC 222, MATH 231, PHYS 115 or PHYS 119; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Principles and Methods of Teaching Earth Science
courses.description: Required preparation: any introductory geology course. This course develops the knowledge and skills teachers need to implement student-centered, inquiry-based earth science instruction at any level level by teaching instructional design and cognitive science and learning theories. Primary literature review and development of lesson modules will be complemented by classroom observations and teaching experiences in formal and informal settings. Course previously offered as GEOL 412.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Systems Modeling
courses.description: This course explores principles and strategies for studying environmental phenomena, and presents methods for developing explanatory and predictive models of environmental systems, e.g., predator-prey, estuaries, greenhouse gases, and ecosystem material cycles.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Meteorology
courses.description: This course explores atmospheric processes most important to environmental problems such as the transport and transformation of air pollutants and weather systems involved in intercontinental transport of gases and particles.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Surface Processes and Landscape Evolution
courses.description: The interplay among the fluxes of water, energy, and sediment through geologic time sculpt landscapes and drive environmental change. In both lectures and laboratory exercises, students will learn how simple physical principles applied to rivers and hillslopes allow us to understand the evolution of topography and mountain belts, predict hazards arising from floods, landslides and debris flows, and lead to sustainable management of natural resources such as soil. Previously offered as GEOL 417.
courses.requisites_raw: Pre- or corequisites, EMES 200 and EMES 201; permission of the instructor for students lacking the pre- or corequisites.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Anthropological Application of GIS
courses.description: This is a beginner/intermediate Geographic Information System/Science (GIS/GISci) course designed to help students develop spatial analysis and data visualization skills using ArcGIS Pro software. The emphasis is on understanding the structure and efficient storage of GIS data (feature classes and geodatabases) and how to work with multiple different types of spatial data (vector, raster, and tabular). Students learn geoprocessing techniques to transform data based on spatial relationships; different methods to classify data based on attributes; and how to perform basic calculations using spatial geometry. This is done through lectures and weekly labs using real world data.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Community Design and Green Architecture
courses.description: The impact of building on the environment and health will be examined by looking at the major areas of: land use planning, water resource use, energy, materials and indoor environment.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Textiles: Environmental Impacts, Issues, and Innovations
courses.description: Textiles are pervasive in our lives, from clothing to upholstery, yet have major impacts on our environment and health, from the products' cradle to grave. This course examines the environmental and social costs of producing our clothing, carpet, and other textiles in daily life. We will also consider possible solutions currently offered by industry and entrepreneurs.
courses.requisites_raw: Pre- or co-requisite, ENEC 201 or 202; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: ENEC 421. | 3 Credits. | Pre- or co-requisite, ENEC 201 or 202; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | FC-CREATE.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Greenhouse Gas Accounting and Carbon Offsets
courses.description: In this class, students will learn the principles of greenhouse gas accounting and how to use them to establish inventories and calculate carbon footprints for products, services, businesses or institutions. We will review the mechanisms of calculating the impact of the most common greenhouse gases, introduce the governing principles for establishing greenhouse gas inventories, as well as the life cycle approach for products and services. Finally, in the last part of the course, we will explore the different types of carbon offsets, including existing and emerging approaches, as well as the risks and opportunities associated with carbon offsets.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ENEC 201, ENEC 202, MATH 110, MATH 130.
requisites_notes: comma-separated list without a conjunction was read as AND

source.text: ENEC 430. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENEC 201 , ENEC 202, MATH 110 , MATH 130 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Sustainable Cities: Exploring Ways of Making Cities More Sustainable
courses.description: Recommended preparation, ENEC 330 . For the first time in history, a majority of the world's people live in cities with huge implications for sustainability. Students will examine the factors driving the trend toward urbanization worldwide, the challenges posed by this trend, and the efforts by cities to become more sustainable.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Life Cycle Assessment
courses.description: Recommended preparation, ENEC 201 , and MATH 110 or 130 . This class will introduce students to environmental life cycle assessment (LCA). The methodology to calculate the environmental impacts associated with a product, a service, or a system will be reviewed through case studies in the field of energy systems, waste management, and eco-design. Students will also get a chance to learn how to perform a full LCA through a hands-on project using LCA software and databases.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Wetland Hydrology
courses.description: Study of wetland ecosystems with particular emphasis on hydrological functioning, the transition from terrestrial to aquatic systems, wetlands as filtration systems, and exchange between wetlands and other environments. Course previously offered as MASC 433.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Principles of Environmental Consulting: Mechanics of Groundwater Flow
courses.description: Water is an essential resource for all life, and the availability of clean water will become one of the most important socio-political and economic discussions over the coming decades. This course covers fundamentals of groundwater storage, subsurface flow, and contaminant transport, emphasizing the role of groundwater in the hydrologic cycle, the relation of groundwater flow to geologic structure, and the management of contaminated groundwater and drinking water resources. Course previously offered as GEOL 435.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EMES 324; MATH 232; PHYS 114 or 118; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Social Vulnerability to Climate Change
courses.description: How does climate change affect vulnerable human populations? We will attempt to answer a shared research question on this topic by reading the peer-reviewed literature and by conducting a semester-long data analysis project incorporating social and climate data from around the world. This is a course-based undergraduate research experience (CURE).

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Marine Physiological Ecology
courses.description: This course introduces students to the physiological, morphological, and behavioral factors employed by marine organisms to cope with their physical environment. Emphasis will be placed on the response of marine organisms to environmental factors such as seawater temperature, light, water salinity, ocean acidification, etc. Course previously offered as MASC 441.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Marine Phytoplankton
courses.description: For junior and senior science majors or graduate students. Biology of marine photosynthetic protists and cyanobacteria. Phytoplankton evolution, biodiversity, structure, function, biogeochemical cycles and genomics. Harmful algal blooms, commercial products, and climate change. Three lecture/practical session hours per week. Course previously offered as MASC 444. Permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Coastal and Estuarine Ecology
courses.description: This course will provide a foundational introduction to key patterns and underlying concepts in coastal and estuarine community ecology. Leveraging the local environment, the class will primarily focus on the structure and community dynamics of important temperate coastal marine habitats such as salt marshes, oyster reefs, seagrass meadows, and beaches (although the ecological concepts are meant to be transferrable across diverse systems).

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Biogeochemical Processes
courses.description: Principles of chemistry, biology, and geology are applied to analysis of the fate and transport of materials in environmental systems, with an emphasis on those materials that form the most significant cycles. Three lecture hours and one laboratory hour a week. Previously offered as GEOL 450/MASC 450.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, CHEM 101 or permission of instructor.

items.text: permission of instructor

source.text: ENEC 450. | 4 Credits. | Prerequisites, CHEM 101 or permission of instructor. | EMES 450 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Population, Development, and the Environment
courses.description: Introduction to contemporary and historical changes in human population, international development, and the global environment and how these processes interact, drawing on population geography as an organizing framework. Previously offered as GEOG 450.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Ecological Anthropology
courses.description: Examines how human-environmental adaptations shape the economic, social, and cultural lives of hunter-gatherers, pastoralists and agriculturalists. Approaches include optimal foraging theory, political ecology and subsistence risk.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Historical Ecology
courses.description: Historical ecology is a framework for integrating physical, biological, and social science data with insights from the humanities to understand the reciprocal relationship between human activity and the Earth system.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Fundamentals of Ecology
courses.description: Students will develop a comprehensive understanding of the field of ecology, including modern and emerging trends in ecology. They will develop literacy in the fundamental theories and models that capture ecological processes; emphasis will also be placed on the relevance of ecology and ecological research for human society.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, BIOL 201; or BIOL 103, BIOL 104, and BIOL 260.

source.text: ENEC 461. | 4 Credits. | Prerequisites, BIOL 201 ; or BIOL 103 , BIOL 104 , and BIOL 260 . | BIOL 461 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Ecosystem Management
courses.description: Explores the ecological concepts underlying ecosystem management (e.g., genetic and species diversity, stability, resilience, landscape ecology, etc.), the tools used in the approach, and case studies of how communities are implementing ecosystem management.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, BIOL 101.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Corporate Environmental Stewardship
courses.description: This course explores the intersection of business/economic growth and the major sustainability issues affecting the environment and societal well-being and raises questions about business ethics and the moral responsibility of business leaders, consumers, and citizens. Previously offered as ENEC 306. Honors version available.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ENEC 201.

source.text: ENEC 463. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENEC 201 . | FC-GLOBAL or FC-VALUES. | BUSI 463 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Global Biodiversity and Macroecology
courses.description: We will explore global patterns of diversity of plants, animals, fungi, and microbes, and the insights gained by taking a statistical approach to describing these and other broad-scale ecological patterns.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, BIOL 201; or BIOL 103, BIOL 104, and BIOL 260; or permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

items.text: or permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites

source.text: ENEC 465. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, BIOL 201 ; or BIOL 103 , BIOL 104 , and BIOL 260 ; or permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites. | FC-NATSCI or FC-QUANT, RESEARCH. | BIOL 465 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Temporal GIS and Space/Time Geostatistics for the Environment and Public Health
courses.description: Reviews geographical information systems (GIS). Covers geostatistics theory for the interpolation of environmental and health monitoring data across space and time. Uses publicly available water and air quality monitoring data to create maps used for environmental assessment, regulatory compliance analysis, exposure science, and risk analysis.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, MATH 232; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: ENEC 468. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, MATH 232 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | ENVR 468 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Risk Assessment
courses.description: Required preparation, one course in probability and statistics. Use of mathematical models and computer simulation tools to estimate the human health impacts of exposure to environmental pollutants. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Human Impacts on Estuarine Ecosystems
courses.description: A cohesive examination of the human impacts on biological processes in estuarine ecosystems. Laboratory/recitation/field work is included and contributes two credit hours to the course. Taught at off-campus field station.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, CHEM 102.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Business and Finance Fundamentals for Change Makers
courses.description: This course is designed to develop basic finance skills along with familiarity with core business concepts. The goal of the course is to empower non-business majors with the skills and vocabulary required to advance the goals of pro-environment businesses and social entrepreneurs.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Sustainable Coastal Management
courses.description: This course explores the environmental history of the Albemarle estuary and its larger watershed and explores ways in which humans can utilize this region in a more sustainable manner. Taught at off-campus field station.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: The Political Economy of Food
courses.description: This course examines the political and economic dimensions of the food we eat, how it is produced, who eats what, and related social and environmental issues, both domestic and international, affecting the production, pricing, trade, distribution, and consumption of food. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Social Coast: Coastal Law, Management and Human Dimensions
courses.description: Coastal systems are socially constructed places, shaped by human institutions, norms, and decisions. As coastal populations grow, so can conflicts about resource use and development. Mix in climate change, sea level rise, and increased storminess, and the dynamism of "life on the edge" can increase. This course combines legal and socio-cultural approaches to understand coastal systems. It introduces relevant laws and policies, explores resulting management regimes and implications, and moves beyond an understanding of management predicated on regulating human activities to examine how the human dimensions of coasts, including values and perceptions, inform behavior and contribute to policy and decision-making.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Landscape Analysis
courses.description: This course utilizes GIS, GPS, and remote sensing technologies to gather data on geology, watersheds, soils, integrated moisture indices. The class also develops habitat maps and derives species diversity indices. Taught at off-campus field station.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Energy Economics
courses.description: This course develops a core set of principles to understand and evaluate energy markets, policies, and regulations. Topics include oil markets, electric vehicles and CAFÉ standards, pollution permit markets and C02 regulations, and electricity markets.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ECON 101.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Energy and the Environment: A Coastal Perspective
courses.description: Explores coastal and offshore energy issues, including energy demand, present-day and innovative sources of energy to meet that demand, economics, policy, and environmental and human health outcomes of different energy sources. Summer session only; online and field trip hybrid course, with a mandatory 8-day field site component on the Outer Banks. Housing and field activities arranged by the instructor, which will carry a fee. Taught at off-campus field station.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Coastal Resource Economics and Policy
courses.description: This course develops and applies core principles essential to understanding and evaluating coastal environmental policy and renewable resource use. The principles include the economics of pollution, public choice, information and cost-benefit analysis, property rights, incentive-based regulation, and the economics of renewable resources. Includes insights from politics and ethics. Taught at off-campus field station.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ECON 101.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Ecological Processes in Environmental Systems
courses.description: Principles of analysis of the structure and function of ecosystems are applied to environmental phenomena. The link between the biosphere and other environmental compartments is explored through case studies of environmental issues. Three lecture hours and one laboratory hour a week. Taught at off-campus field station.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Special Topics in Environmental Science and Studies
courses.description: Advanced topics from diverse areas of environmental science and/or environmental studies are explored. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Communicating Science in the Anthropocene
courses.description: Science communication is essential in today's world, especially for clear public understanding and decision making. This course teaches students to effectively translate scientific concepts for diverse audiences, from school groups to professionals. Emphasizing creative writing and digital media, students will develop skills in oral presentations, essays, and social media.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Social Science Research Methods
courses.description: Students learn quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods research skills and their application to public policies and management of natural resources.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Internship
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. This course provides an internship with an organization related to environmental sciences or studies. Pass/Fail only.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Policy Analysis of Global Climate Change
courses.description: Provides a real-world and relevant case study in which to apply material from multiple disciplines including public policy, economics, environmental science, and international studies. Teaches techniques for building policy models not covered elsewhere.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Stable Isotopes in the Environment
courses.description: Introduction to the theory, methods, and applications of stable isotopes to environmental problems. Primary focus will be on the origin, natural abundance, and fractionation of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen isotopes. Course previously offered as GEOL 511.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, CHEM 102.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Advanced Coastal Environmental Change
courses.description: This 3-credit seminar-style class for graduate students and advanced undergraduate students focuses on developing a deeper understanding of coastal environmental change as illuminated by the scientific literature, including topics such as climate change impacts; coupled human-natural coastal dynamics; feedbacks between biological and physical processes; carbon storage and flux; adaptive coastal management; and the role of science, policy and communication in coastal resilience. Course previously offered as ENEC 710/GEOL 710/MASC 730.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, EMES 303, 310, 410, 417, or 503; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Change and Human Health
courses.description: The course will provide students with a multidisciplinary perspective of environmental changes to encompass both human health and ecological health.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ENEC 201 or 202.

source.text: ENEC 522. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENEC 201 or 202. | ENVR 522 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Principles of Climate Modeling
courses.description: Recommended preparation, MATH 383 . Develops explanatory and predictive models of the earth's climate. The level is introductory and the emphasis is on modeling past climate with the hope of understanding its future.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, MATH 231, 232, and 233; PHYS 118 and 119.

source.text: ENEC 530. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 231 , 232 , and 233 ; PHYS 118 and 119 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Introduction to Risk Management and Insurance
courses.description: Introduces the motivations, objectives, and principles of financial risk management through the lens of insurance, reinsurance and financial institutions. Students will become familiar with key concepts that shape these industries so they can effectively communicate using industry vocabulary, metrics, and tools. Standards governing financial risk management are introduced as are the different types of risks that financial institutions, insurers and reinsurers analyze when conducting business. Students will make use of software and tools to characterize and price risk in various activities, carry out basic quantitative risk assessments, and learn what drives success and failure in financial risk management.
courses.requisites_raw: Pre- or corequisite, Two or more of the following classes (or permission of the instructor): MATH 231, MATH 232, STOR 151, STOR 155, BIOS 511, BIOS 512, BIOS 600, ECON 400, BIOL/ ENEC 562.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Natural Hazards and Financial Risk
courses.description: Society's growing exposure to the financial risks associated with natural hazards (e.g., flood, drought, extreme temperatures) has made it increasingly important to both accurately quantify these risks and develop innovative strategies for managing them. This course provides exposure to the fundamentals of financial risk management with application to natural hazards an emphasis on developing coupled models that consider natural variability, engineered/managed structures and financial/economic factors. Students will learn to (i) model the financial risk posed by extreme events; (ii) understand the merits of various risk management tools; and (iii) develop effective strategies for managing natural hazard-based financial risk.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Risk, Data Science and AI
courses.description: Students are introduced to advanced techniques in data sciences, machine learning, and artificial intelligence and their application to the management of financial risks. Students will learn to discover, process, and visualize natural hazard and financial data, and will be taught to quantify various financial risks (e.g., natural hazards) and design management strategies to mitigate negative outcomes. Students will learn basic programming methods and apply data analysis and machine learning techniques to model the complex systems that give rise to risk. Structured case studies and in-class assignments will help students build expertise to be used in longer group projects.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Innovation in Risk Management and Insurance
courses.description: The course focuses on understanding the complex challenges the RMI industry is facing and how to think innovatively from various perspectives to solve them. Many factors are challenging the insurance industry today, including: 1) uncertainty surrounding inflation and interest rates; 2) new regulations to protect customers and avoid systemic risk; 3) consumer demand for radically different customer experiences; and 4) high technology, which is introducing new rules and strengthening competition. Students will develop knowledge and skills to understand how these elements affect the RMI industry, critically analyze them, and develop novel ideas to solve them.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, At least two of the following courses: MATH 231, MATH 232, STOR 151, STOR 155, BIOS 511, BIOS 512, BIOS 600, ECON 400, BIOL/ ENEC 562; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the requisite.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Managing Risk, Return, and Reserves
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for students lacking the requisite. This course is designed to give undergraduate and graduate students exposure to the challenges of managing the financial risk of uncertainty in the value of liabilities and assets within an insurance/reinsurance/risk management context. Students will learn to use actuarial and financial market data to make risk-based decisions related to setting insurance premiums and allocating assets based on estimates of future liabilities (e.g., claims, market losses). The course will introduce students to the properties of different asset classes and hedging tools and demonstrate different methods to assemble portfolios that balance profitability with the risk of insolvency.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Modeling Catastrophe Risk & Resilience
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the physical processes, statistical methods, and analytical tools used to assess risks that arise from natural hazard events, with an emphasis on extreme precipitation (floods) and hurricanes. Students will examine the dynamics of extreme weather events and hydrologic hazards, learn modern approaches to extreme value analysis, and work with real-world datasets and industry tools to build models of financial risk. Some programming experience is helpful but not required. Previously offered as EMES 414/ENEC 514/GEOL 514.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, Any two of the following: MATH 231, MATH 232, STOR 151, STOR 155, BIOS 511, BIOS 512, BIOS 600, ECON 400, BIOL/ ENEC 562 or equivalent, or instructor permission.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Energy, Transportation, and Land Use
courses.description: This course explores the reciprocal connections between energy (production/conversion, distribution, and use), land use, environment, and transportation. Evaluation of federal, state, and local policies on energy conservation and alternative energy sources are emphasized. Students gain skills to analyze impacts, interdependencies, and uncertainties of various energy conservation measures and production technologies.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Sustainable Energy Systems
courses.description: This course will provide an introduction to urgent topics related to energy, sustainability, and the environment. The course material will focus on new technologies, policies, and plans in cities and different governing bodies in the energy system with a focus on developing tools to analyze energy for its sustainability, impact on people, the environment, and the economy.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Statistics for Environmental Scientists
courses.description: Introduction to the application of quantitative and statistical methods in environmental science, including environmental monitoring, assessment, threshold exceedance, risk assessment, and environmental decision making.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, BIOL 103 and BIOL 104, and either STOR 120 or STOR 155; or permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

items.text: or permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Statistical Analysis in Ecology and Evolution
courses.description: Application of modern statistical analysis and data modeling in ecological and evolutionary research. Emphasis is on computer-intensive methods and model-based approaches. Familiarity with standard parametic statistics is assumed.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, BIOL 103, BIOL 104, MATH 231, and either STOR 120 or STOR 155; or permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

items.text: or permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Storytelling
courses.description: An interdisciplinary course for students interested in environmental issues or journalism to produce stories about environmental issues that matter to North Carolinians. Students learn to identify credible sources, manage substantial amounts of information, and find story focus as they report on technical and often controversial subjects in a variety of media.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Ecological Analyses and Application
courses.description: This course provides an overview of natural and social science approaches to addressing biodiversity conservation and resource management. Concepts and methods from population biology, evolutionary ecology, community ecology, and conservation biology will be complemented with approaches from common property theory, indigenous resource management, and human evolutionary ecology.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Current Issues in Ecology
courses.description: Required preparation, previous course work in ecology. Permission of the instructor. Topics vary but focus on interdisciplinary problems facing humans and/or the environment. May be repeated for credit.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Uncertainty, Decisions, and the Environment
courses.description: Required preparation, one course in probability and statistics. Use of quantitative tools for balancing conflicting priorities (such as costs versus human health protection) and evaluating uncertainties when making environmental decisions.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Markets: Science and Economics
courses.description: Examines the interplay of science and economics in the design of environmental markets. The first part introduces the principles of environmental economics. The second part considers several case studies that illustrate the critical role that scientific models of natural systems play in the design of environmental markets.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Water Resource Planning and Policy Analysis
courses.description: Water resources demand-supply relationships, United States water resource and related water quality policy, legal structure for water allocation, planning, project and program evaluation, and pricing. Strategies for coping with floods, droughts, and climate change will be explored. Extensive use of case studies.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Water Quality Policies and Planning
courses.description: Introduction to the management of water quality at the local and basinwide scales. Topics include theory and management frameworks; state and federal statutes and programs; water contaminants, their fate and transport; alternatives for improving and protecting water quality; and the technologies and management practices of selected basinwide comprehensive strategies.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, BIOL 101 and MATH 231.

source.text: ENEC 586. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, BIOL 101 and MATH 231 .

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Practicum
courses.description: Permission of the instructor required. Students receive service-learning credit through active participation in a community, campus, or other approved group project.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Professional Development Skills for Ecologists and Biologists
courses.description: The goal of this course is to help students who intend to become professional ecologists or biologists acquire critical skills and strategies needed for achieving their career goals.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Continuum Mechanics in the Earth Sciences
courses.description: Applications of continuum mechanics in the earth sciences, including stress, strain, elasticity, and viscous flow. Numerical solutions to problems in heterogeneous finite strain including finite element analysis. Course previously offered as GEOL 608.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, EMES 302, and PHYS 114 or 118.

courses.title: Energy Modeling for Environment and Public Health
courses.description: Recommended preparation, MATH 231 . This course will equip students with an overview of contemporary issues in energy modeling and energy systems analysis, with a focus on environmental and public health impacts of energy systems. Students will gain exposure to a variety of research methodologies, analytical tools, and applications of energy modeling applied to environmental and public health related problems such as climate change, air pollution, and water footprints of energy systems.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Watershed Planning
courses.description: This course explores the functions of ecosystems, land development activities that impact such functions, and the land use management tools to create strategies for mitigating and restoring environmental damage. Course goals include understanding the ecological context of planning and how ecological principles may inform planning decisions. Prepares planners to engage effectively with biologists, natural resource managers, park managers, and other professionals from the natural sciences.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental Communication and the Public Sphere
courses.description: Examines communication practices that accompany citizen participation in environmental decisions, including public education campaigns of nonprofit organizations, "risk communication," media representations, and mediation in environmental disputes.

courses.subject: ENEC
courses.title: Environmental and Resource Economics
courses.description: Theory and methods of environmental economics. Topics covered include cost-benefit analysis and environmental policy analysis, economic concept of sustainability, optimal use of natural resources, nonmarket valuation, and economic instruments.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ECON 310.
